Alan Bishop was a good second in the 880 yds., which was won in 2 min. 1.5 secs., while Stan Davies and George Stace scored in the 1 mile. Our juniors won their 4 x 110 relay but the seniors were just beaten in a close finish in the closing darkness.
Doug Briggs and George Stace spoke most ably in their own defence, but at the same time did not disagree with the necessity for having an organised run with the pack once a week.
The handicap was won by George Stace, with "Jumbo" Masters in second place and Denis Brickwood third, and Masters ran very well seeing that this was his first appearance over the country this season.

The individual race was won easily by "Lofty" Holden, of Cambridge H., and our first man home was Bob Taylor, 17th, our other scorers being Mick Porter, 27; John Burr, 32; Ray Tooby, 38; Len Bishop, 57, and George Stace, 61.

Bob Taylor was 2nd in the 1 mile, with John Burr 3rd, and George Stace ran well to win the 2 miles run in 9 mins. 58 secs. We also won the 1 miles medley relay, with Jim Heathfield, Bob Wolton, Ron Morrell and Ivan Mayers.
Davidson, George Stace, S. Gawler, John Burr, Peter Courtney, Eric Gebbett, and " Spud " Abbott, and all these were inside the 1st-class standard time of 15 mins. 45secs.

Eric Bishop was 3rd in the mile and George Stace was similarly placed in the 2 miles event with his best performance to date. In the latter race we had Tom Carter in action and although his speed is not of former years his style is as good as ever.

It was a poor day for running with very heavy rain during the early stages of the race, particularly when George Stace was running. We were well back on the first leg, but were brought from 9th to 2nd during the next two legs.
Dave Hooper ran a well judged race to finish 2nd in the three miles with George Stace 3rd. Llewellyn of Walton won the mile in 4.24.2, closely followed by Davidson and Roffey.

The end of the first lap saw George Stace and Len Bishop were leading with several other teams within striking distance. This pair however, could not maintain their position and soon a terrific battle was taking place with Eric Gebbet paired that Alan Black and Bill Bird paired with Jim Edgar.
